subject: Is there a Response to Barry & Welsh (2001)?

messages.author: 3bbe9e00c88a70b2
messages.subject: Is there a Response to Barry & Welsh (2001)?
parts:
Regarding the paper by Barry & Welsh (2001) Distance sampling methodology.
Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B, 63:31-53. I believe that
Rachel Fewster presented a review of the flaws in this paper at the 2001
ICODS (but the website with conference abstracts is currently unavailable)
-- has there ever been anything published in the peer-reviewed literature? I
could not find anything.



This paper and another by Welsh (2002) Australia and New Zealand Journal of
Statistics 44:13-22 are the only papers I know of that suggest statistical
flaws with distance sampling. Is that correct?



Duane

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Is there a Response to Barry & Welsh (2001)?
parts:
There is also a Biometrics paper, Melville and Welsh:

Melville, G. J. and Welsh, A. H. (2001). Line transect sampling in small
regions. Bio-
metrics 57, 1130-1137.

Biometrics allowed us to respond - the authors' response to our response
has a couple of rather silly errors! Our response is at

Fewster, R.M., Laake, J.L. and Buckland, S.T. 2005. Line transect
sampling in small and large regions. /Biometrics/ *61*, 856-859.

Series B wouldn't contemplate publishing any response - so not even the
mathematical errors in Barry and Welsh have been corrected! However,
the following articles are relevant:

Fewster, R.M. and Buckland, S.T. 2004. Assessment of distance sampling
estimators. In /Advanced Distance Sampling/, pp281-306. S.T. Buckland,
D.R. Anderson, K.P. Burnham, J.L. Laake, D.L. Borchers and L. Thomas
(eds). Oxford University Press, Oxford.

Fewster, R.M., Southwell, C., Borchers, D.L., Buckland, S.T. and Pople,
A.R. 2008. The influence of animal mobility on the assumption of
uniform distances in aerial line transect surveys. /Wildlife Research/
*35*, 275-288.

Fewster, R.M., Buckland, S.T., Burnham, K.P., Borchers, D.L., Jupp,
P.E., Laake, J.L. and Thomas, L. in press. Estimating the encounter
rate variance in distance sampling. /Biometrics/.

The ANZJS article was so over the top, it didn't merit any response!

Steve Buckland
